### Trail Dossier: Cabana Malaiesti (from Gura Diham via Pichetul Rosu)

#### 1. Quick Summary
- Mountain Massif: Bucegi Mountains
- Starting Point: Gura Diham Chalet (accessible by car from Busteni)
- Official Marking: Red Stripe (Gura Diham to Pichetul Rosu), then Red Dot (Pichetul Rosu to Malaiesti)
- Difficulty Level: Moderate (accessible for moderate hikers, requires patience for steady elevation gain)
- Estimated Duration: 5 - 6 hours round-trip
- Elevation Gain: +650 m / -650 m

#### 2. Itinerary and Waypoints
- Stage 1: Gura Diham Chalet -> Pichetul Rosu (1.5 - 2 hours, gradual ascent through beech and fir forest via Red Stripe marking)
- Stage 2: Pichetul Rosu -> Cabana Malaiesti (1.5 hours, contour trail crossing valleys and ridges via Red Dot marking)
- Return Route: Same path in reverse (Descent from Cabana Malaiesti back to Gura Diham via Pichetul Rosu in approximately 2.5 - 3 hours)
- Water Sources and Mountain Huts / Shelters: Potable water is available at Gura Diham Chalet and at Cabana Malaiesti. 

#### 3. Weather and Ridge Conditions
- Condition: Mainly clear
- Temperature: 4.7 C (Apparent temperature: 1.5 C)
- Wind: 9.2 km/h with gusts up to 40.3 km/h
- Precipitation: 0.0 mm
- Visibility: Good
- Salvamont Hazard Alerts: Conditions within standard mountain safety limits, but always anticipate sudden weather shifts in the afternoon.

#### 4. Hazards, Difficulties and Salvamont Safety Rules
- Technical sections: Generally well-maintained forest paths, but watch your step on wet tree roots or loose gravel sections along the traverse.
- Wildlife awareness (bear encounter conduct): Remain calm, speak firmly, back away slowly, and never run. Bucegi forests are active bear habitats.
- Time management: Start your hike early in the morning. Even as a self-described lazy hiker, you must allow yourself a generous daylight buffer so you do not descend in the dark.

#### 5. Recommended Gear Checklist
- Sturdy hiking boots with solid grip (Vibram sole recommended)
- Layered synthetic clothing (avoid cotton), waterproof and windproof jacket
- Minimum 1.5 - 2L water per person plus energy snacks
- Reliable headlamp with extra batteries, portable power bank
- First aid kit and emergency survival foil
- Spare warm fleece or insulating layer for when you rest at the cabin

#### 6. Mountain Emergency Contacts (Salvamont)

- European Emergency Number: 112
